shared_params.picks_b: Comma-separated draft picks on side B.

shared_params.legs: JSON array of trade legs: [{'from','to','players','picks'}], players as comma-separated names or array, picks as [{'year','round','swap','protection'}]. Outgoing first-round picks are duplicate-checked and validated at year grain against silver_future_picks when seeded; protection/swap reconciliation and pooled/conditional picks are not modeled; same-year multiple firsts are validated only at year grain because the leg input does not identify the original team of a same-year first.
shared_params.sign_and_trade: JSON object for a sign-and-trade piece: {'player','new_salary','years'}; new_salary and years must be positive integers. The CBA term must be 3-4 seasons; first-season full guarantee required by 2023 CBA Art. VII sec. 8(e)(1) is not validated; prior-team and preseason eligibility are not modeled; years is treated as total declared seasons; non-option seasons cannot be distinguished, so option-year treatment is unsupported.
shared_params.cash: JSON array of cash movements: [{'from','to','amount'}]. Amounts must be positive integers, and both endpoints must be trade parties; the annual cash ledger is not tracked.
shared_params.tpe: JSON array of declared traded-player-exception uses: [{'team','amount','kind','origin_season'|'origin_year','origin_date','expiry_date'}]. kind is optional: ordinary accepts the standard alias, and sign_and_trade accepts sign_and_trade_generated, snt and snt_generated. Use origin_season in consecutive-year YYYY-YY form or origin_year as the season-start year; they must agree if both are present. Optional origin_date/expiry_date are YYYY-MM-DD exact dates. origin_date uses the July-June league year, must agree with origin season/year when both are supplied, and derives a one-year expiry when expiry_date is omitted; expiry_date must be after origin_date. Present keys must be non-null; amount/origin_year are strict JSON integers (bool/float rejected). Amount-only legacy rows default to ordinary current-season uses and return legacy_defaults. Exact expiry deadlines remain usable through their dates and expire only afterward; weekend and federal-holiday deadlines roll to the following business day; season-only rows use approximate legacy season bins where current/prior origins are active, older expire and future entries are unavailable; each active row is a separate amount+$250k capacity bin (cushion $0 over first apron) and cannot combine with salary or another TPE for one acquisition.
shared_params.evaluation_date: Exact evaluation date ISO YYYY-MM-DD; blank uses the league date in America/New_York.
shared_params.tpes: JSON array of traded-player-exception rows: [{'team','amount','kind','origin_year'}]; amount integer dollars, kind ordinary or sign_and_trade. Rows represent exceptions the user explicitly carries into the evaluation — never auto-derived league state.

tools.name: sql_exec
tools.description:
Run one agent-written read-only analytical query over the warehouse.

The query must be a single SELECT or WITH statement over the declared
silver tables. Writes, stacked statements, and tables outside the
declared set are refused before execution. DESCRIBE, SHOW TABLES,
information_schema and catalog functions are refused as well; call
warehouse_schema for table and column listings. Results are capped at
RERUN_ROW_CAP rows with a RERUN_TIMEOUT_S statement timeout; a valid
query returning 0 rows returns ok=True, rows=[], row_count=0, and
meta.empty_observation=True (unless DIME_STRICT_NONEMPTY_SQL=1).
Name the primary numeric column for what it measures, so a percentage
answers as TS_PCT and a count as `n`; the column you alias is the
column a citation binds to.

Every ok result also carries meta.basis and meta.profile. If you need
a contributor count for an expression such as AVG, or distinct-value
counts, add COUNT(metric) or COUNT(DISTINCT x) columns to your query.
guidelines: Use for ad-hoc read-only SELECT/WITH analysis over declared silver tables when no specialized tool returns the needed grain. Do not use for writes, live sources, or Python-only reshaping; rows are query-grain output and declared units/season encodings must be preserved.

tools.name: warehouse_schema
tools.schema_description: Read declared warehouse columns, source units and season encodings.
guidelines: Use before sql_exec or when columns, units, or season encodings are uncertain, especially with scoped table selection. Do not use as proof of freshness or complete inventory; catalog_scope limits negative claims to returned declared tables and columns.

tools.name: get_rapm
tools.description: RAPM-lite ratings. Blank player returns top list, else one row.
tools.schema_description: RAPM-lite ratings. Blank player returns top list, else one row.
guidelines: Use for RAPM-lite player ratings or a top list when a documented impact rating is needed. Do not treat blank-player output as a complete roster or compare across seasons without checking season and minimums; values are per-possession rating units.

tools.name: get_impact_rank
tools.description: Player impact and league rank for a season across all-in-one plus-minus metrics the warehouse covers: published BPM (basketball-reference advanced), rapm-lite estimates, and FiveThirtyEight RAPTOR for older seasons. One row per metric covering the season; rank is 1..N by value within that season's player pool. Player required; season optional. Warehouse only; each row cites its source.

tools.name: get_game_prediction
tools.description: Pre-game Monte Carlo prediction: win probability, projected score/total, and confidence intervals. Model estimates with documented methodology, not betting picks. Two team names/abbrevs/ids; optional game_date (MM/DD/YYYY), n_sims, seed for reproducibility.
tools.schema_description: Pre-game Monte Carlo prediction: win probability, projected score/total, and confidence intervals.
guidelines: Use for pre-game Monte Carlo win probability, projected score/total, and intervals for two teams. Do not treat as betting picks or actual results; outputs are model estimates with simulation parameters.

tools.name: get_wpa_leaders
tools.description:
WPA-by-play leaderboard for one season. Season is an end-year clamped to 2021..2025.

Deltas come from the fitted win-probability model before and after
each play, credited to the acting player. Documented estimates.
tools.schema_description: WPA-by-play leaderboard for one season.

tools.name: get_comps
tools.description: Nearest statistical neighbors by per-36 + advanced shape. Same-season only.
tools.schema_description: Nearest statistical neighbors by per-36 + advanced shape. Same-season only.
guidelines: Use for same-season nearest statistical neighbors by per-36 and advanced shape. Do not use as cross-era or career comps or causal peer groups; outputs are similarity-ranked player-season rows.

tools.name: get_era_comps
tools.description: Cross-era statistical neighbors for one player's season. Compares the target season's per-36 box-score shape and efficiency profile against every qualified player-season in the warehouse (1996-97 onward), with each feature z-scored within its own season so the match is era-relative shape, not raw level. Optional start_season/end_season window (e.g. '2003-04' to '2010-11') narrows the candidate pool. Same-season-only comps live in get_comps.
tools.schema_description: Cross-era statistical neighbors for one player season, z-scored within each season (1996-97+).

tools.name: get_lineup_stats
tools.description:
Per-unit five-man lineup ratings with possession floors for one team. Names, abbrevs, or ids. For all qualifying units sorted by minutes use get_lineups; for the league-wide board use get_lineup_leaders.

Units under min_possessions (default 100) are hidden; blowout-heavy
units are flagged. Ratings are per 100 possessions, warehouse-first.
The best lineup (highest NET_RATING among units meeting the floor) is
returned in the top-level best_net_unit field and flagged per-row as
is_best_net_unit, so it is never the most-used unit by default.
For a player on-versus-off split (not unit ratings) use get_on_off or
get_on_off_leaders.
tools.schema_description: Five-man lineup ratings with sample floors. Names, abbrevs, or ids.
guidelines: Use for one team's five-man lineup ratings after sample floors. Do not compare raw plus/minus without checking possessions, minutes, or sample flags; rows are lineup-season units rated per 100 possessions.

tools.name: get_lineup_on_off
tools.description:
On/off-court splits for an arbitrary 2-5 player combination on one team, computed from possession-level data. Names or ids, comma-separated. For single-player splits use get_on_off; for a named two-player pair use get_wowy; for whole-lineup ratings use get_lineup_stats.

Returns possessions, points for/against, and per-100 OFF/DEF/NET ratings
for the unit together versus all other possessions by that team, plus
the on-minus-off delta. Possessions flagged as garbage time are excluded.
Units under min_possessions (default 100) are flagged as tiny-sample, not
dropped; blowout-heavy splits are flagged at the same share rule as
get_lineup_stats.

tools.name: get_win_prob
tools.description: Real ELO win probability between two abbreviations. Neutral unless home_abbrev matches a side.
tools.schema_description: Real ELO win probability between two abbreviations. Neutral unless home_abbrev matches a side.
guidelines: Use for a quick real-ELO win probability between two team abbreviations. Do not use for matchup analysis or when home court matters unless home_abbrev is set; output is a single probability.

tools.name: get_on_off
tools.description:
Single-player on/off-court splits for one team, possession level: the team's OFF/DEF/NET rating per 100 possessions with the player on the floor versus off, the on-minus-off gap, and the possession count in each bucket.

REACH FOR THIS for 'how does the team do when X sits', 'does the team fall apart without X', 'net rating with X on vs off', 'on-minus-off gap' asks — it returns the answer-shaped split directly. For a 2-5 player combination split use get_lineup_on_off; for a named two-player 2x2 use get_wowy or get_on_off_leaders; for game-level record when a player SAT OUT entirely (missed games, not minutes) use get_availability_impact; for five-man unit ratings use get_lineup_stats.
tools.schema_description: On and off splits for one player on one team. Possession level.
guidelines: Use for one player's on/off possession-level splits on one team. Do not attribute lineup effects to the player alone or ignore opponent and teammate context; rows are stat-split units from warehouse possessions.

tools.name: get_availability_impact
tools.description: Game-level availability impact: split a team's results into the games a player played versus the games they missed (game counts, record, win pct, average margin). Pass a player for the single-player split; add teammate to split that player's own per-game scoring/FGA/plus-minus by the teammate's presence; or leave player empty for a league-wide ranking of high-minute one-team players by win-rate drop when sitting (min_minutes/min_missed qualifiers). Warehouse coverage: 2015-16 onward, regular season. Possession-level net rating with the player on vs off the floor is a different question — use get_on_off (one player) or get_on_off_leaders (boards and pairs).
tools.schema_description: Game-level availability splits: a team's record, win pct, and average margin in games a player played vs missed; optional teammate-presence per-game scoring split; or a league-wide win-drop ranking when player is blank. Warehouse 2015-16+.

params.teammate: Optional second player; splits the first player's own per-game PTS/FGA/plus-minus by this teammate's presence. Default: {d}.
params.min_missed: Ranking mode only: minimum games missed to qualify. Default: {d}.

tools.name: get_on_off_leaders
tools.description: Stint-level on/off splits from the possessions warehouse. Modes: pass player + team for one player's on/off split (per-100 OFF/DEF/NET each way); pass team alone for that team's board ranked by on-court possessions; pass pair as 'A,B' (+ team if known) for a two-player 2x2 (both on / each alone / both off); pass neither for a league board of qualifying players ranked by on-minus-off net gap (min_on_possessions/min_off_possessions floors). Use for 'better/worse with X on the floor', on-off net rating gaps, and rotation-impact asks. Coverage 2009-10 onward, regular season.
tools.schema_description: Stint-level on/off splits: league board ranked by on-minus-off net gap with possession floors, one team's board by on-court possessions, a single player's on/off split, or a two-player 2x2. Warehouse silver_stints 2009-10+.

params.pair: Two players as 'A,B' for a 2x2 split (both on / each alone / both off). Default: {d}.
params.team: Team name, abbreviation, or id. With player: that player's split; alone: team board by on-court possessions. Default: {d}.
params.min_on_possessions: League board only: minimum on-court possessions to qualify. Default: {d}.
params.min_off_possessions: League board only: minimum off-court possessions to qualify. Default: {d}.

tools.name: get_shot_zones
tools.description:
Zone splits for one player id: rim, midrange, three with shares.

Warehouse-first: historical silver_hist_shots geometric zones, then
seeded silver_shots, then seeded silver_zone_splits
(basketball-reference distance buckets, league-wide), then live
shot_chart (fail-fast; endpoint-blocked from datacenter IPs).
Zones below min_attempts (default 50, clamped 10..200) are excluded. Zones here are geometric court regions, not basketball-reference distance buckets: when the ask names silver_zone_splits or distance buckets (0-3ft, 3-10ft, 10-16ft, 16ft-3pt, 3pt), query silver_zone_splits via sql_exec instead.
tools.schema_description: Zone splits for one player id: rim, midrange, three with shares.
guidelines: Use for one player's shot-zone volume and efficiency shares by zone. Do not use for team diet or shot-level examples; zones below min_attempts are excluded and values are zone-level FG/eFG shares.

tools.name: get_phase_shot_splits
tools.description: Regular season vs playoffs shooting splits for one player or team in one season: zone diet and eFG plus shot-family splits (catch-and-shoot vs pull-up vs rim) with playoff-minus-regular deltas in percentage points. Warehouse-first from silver_hist_shots; measured tracking splits appear when seeded. Give exactly one of player or team. Zones here are geometric court regions, not basketball-reference distance buckets: when the ask names silver_zone_splits or distance buckets (0-3ft, 3-10ft, 10-16ft, 16ft-3pt, 3pt), query silver_zone_splits via sql_exec instead.
tools.schema_description: Regular season vs playoffs shooting splits for one player or team: zone eFG/share plus catch-and-shoot vs pull-up family splits with deltas and cited warehouse sources.

tools.name: get_four_factors
tools.description:
Team four factors (eFG%, TOV%, ORB%, FT rate, plus defensive
mirrors), computed offline from warehouse team game rows. Use for
"why are the Thunder good", "team identity", or any four-factors
ask. Pass a team name/abbrev to scope to one team; empty returns
the full 30-team board.
tools.schema_description: Team four factors breakdown (eFG%, TOV%, ORB%, FT rate, plus defensive mirrors).

tools.name: get_clutch_stats
tools.description: Clutch stats (last 5 min, margin 5 or less), player or team scope.
tools.schema_description: NBA clutch statistics (last 5 min, margin <= 5) for player or team scope.

tools.name: get_competitive_ratings
tools.description:
Competitive MOV: what happens to a team's MOV when blowouts are dropped.

team: 3-letter abbrev, full name, nickname, city, or "league"/"" for
all teams. season: "YYYY-YY" or "all" for every warehouse season
(multi-season output is pooled across seasons, not a single
team-season -- see meta.season_note). season_type: regular (default),
playoffs, or all; matched against the actual distinct warehouse values
before aggregating. NOTE: the default changed from "all" to "regular"
on 2026-09-10 so season-scoped queries no longer silently mix playoff
games in; pass "all" explicitly to include playoffs.
blowout_margin: games with abs(plus_minus) above this are excluded from
the competitive set (clamped to [1, 40]). min_games: floor on
competitive games; rows below it are flagged low_sample and carry
numbers with no interpretation. Warehouse only; plus_minus is each
team's own MOV per game.
tools.schema_description: Competitive Margin of Victory (MOV excluding blowouts).

tools.name: get_news_feed
tools.description: Recent NBA news items from warehouse-seeded RSS feeds (headline, published, url, players/teams mentioned). Optional team abbreviation or player-name filter. Reads the warehouse only; refresh with seed_injury_news.py.

tools.name: get_team_daily_brief

tools.name: get_award_results

Recorded NBA award results read from published ballots.

view=winner returns every subject sharing the leading rank for one award in
one season. view=winner_history returns the leading-rank subject(s) for that
award in every covered season through the requested season. view=field returns
the whole ranked ballot with vote shares and vote counts. view=player_awards
returns one player's award record through the named season. Use get_award_race
for a model score, never for a result.

tools.description: Morning briefing: scoreboard plus top scorers. Date MM/DD/YYYY, blank means latest.
tools.schema_description: Morning briefing: scoreboard plus top scorers. Date MM/DD/YYYY, blank means latest.

tools.description: League standings for one season like 2025-26.
tools.schema_description: NBA regular-season conference and league standings for any season.

This is a trajectory evidence primitive, not a trend opinion. It reads

tools.schema_description: Multi-season regular-season records and win percentages for any team.

tools.name: get_ratings

Team ratings, optionally bound to one requested ranked metric.

When ``requested_metric`` and ``ranking_direction`` are set, rows are
ordered by that metric field and the payload owns the leader claim.
``team`` narrows a direct team-ratings question.
tools.schema_description: Team offensive, defensive, net ratings, and pace (league-wide or team specific).

tools.name: get_rookie_leaders
tools.description:
Current rookie class leaderboard (first-year NBA players only).

Rookies are defined structurally: a player in the current-season
stats table with NO row in any prior season (hist or warehouse).
Never an age proxy, never historical seasons (F46: a "rookies 20+
ppg" query answered from 2023-24 listed Edwards/LaMelo/Wemby; the
right answer was the current draft class, e.g. Cooper Flagg).
stat is a per-game column: ppg, rpg, apg, spg, bpg, mpg.
tools.schema_description: Current rookie class leaderboard (first-year NBA players only, verified against historical seasons).

tools.name: get_cap_ledger
tools.description: Payroll plus apron room for one abbreviation. 2026-27 thresholds. Payroll/apron values use the warehouse salary ledger as a proxy for exact Apron Team Salary; bonus, dead-money, roster-status, exception-inventory, free-agent/tender, and offseason adjustments are not computable, so apron and hard-cap conclusions are screening estimates near either apron.
tools.schema_description: Payroll, luxury tax position, and first/second apron room for one team. Payroll/apron values are a salary-ledger proxy for exact Apron Team Salary, so apron and hard-cap conclusions are screening estimates near either apron.
guidelines: Use for one team's payroll, cap space, luxury tax, and apron-room snapshot under declared CBA thresholds. Do not use for trade legality or player value; figures are season-specific ledger totals, not per-game rates.

tools.name: get_cap_scenario
tools.description: Cap-scenario arithmetic for one team. "signings" takes comma-separated amounts or name=amount pairs like "Player=12M, 3000000"; this compatibility grammar is validated as mechanism auto with a one-year term and cannot represent chronological ordering or declared exception state. "in_players" adds real contracts by name (league-wide lookup). "trade_out_players" removes roster salary only when those players are actually traded away. "waive_players" waives roster players; guaranteed money remains as estimated dead cap. "stretch" uses the CBA two-times-years-plus-one estimate; player-option years count and team-option years do not. Optional "waiver_date" (YYYY-MM-DD inside the scenario league year) selects the timing branch; blank uses the July 1-Aug 31 pre-Sep-1 branch and discloses that default. In the Sep 1-Jun 30 branch the current-season allocation is unchanged and only future-season salary is stretched. The retired "out_players" input is rejected because it hid that distinction. Guarantee data is a remaining-contract pool, not per-year allocations. Returns the arithmetic trace, post-move payroll vs cap/tax/first/second apron, the 2023 CBA restrictions that trigger, and the matching verdict when a trade portion is present. REACH FOR THIS for any "can X afford/sign Y" or "what if they waive/trade for Z" ask: "can the Warriors sign Player for $12M?", "what happens to Phoenix payroll if they waive Beal?", "does taking back $30M push DEN over the second apron?" It computes post-move apron status and CBA restrictions directly - do not rebuild that arithmetic from get_cap_ledger rows. Payroll/apron values use the warehouse salary ledger as a proxy for exact Apron Team Salary; bonus, dead-money, roster-status, exception-inventory, free-agent/tender, and offseason adjustments are not computable, so apron and hard-cap conclusions are screening estimates near either apron. Legality rows expose matching_structure, matching_mechanisms, expanded_required, and a matching_note inferred as the least restrictive available simultaneous structure; they do not model actual trade-call exception elections or prior hard-cap history.
tools.schema_description: Cap-scenario arithmetic: post-move payroll vs cap/tax/aprons plus the 2023 CBA restrictions that trigger, for hypothetical signings and player moves on one team. Signing validation is mechanism-aware but approximate, not exact CBA legality. Payroll/apron values are a salary-ledger proxy for exact Apron Team Salary, so apron and hard-cap conclusions are screening estimates near either apron. Rows expose the inferred least-restrictive simultaneous matching structure and whether expanded matching is required.

tools.name: get_trade_check
tools.description:
Trade legality check. Player names comma separated per side.

2023 CBA simultaneous salary matching: standard matching covers up to 100 percent of outgoing salary plus a $250k cushion, with the cushion reduced to $0 over the first apron. Above that standard band, expanded matching uses 200 percent plus 250k when outgoing is up to 8.846M, outgoing plus 9.096M up to 35.384M, or 125 percent plus 250k above that. 100 percent exact matching applies above the first apron, with no aggregation above the second apron. Expanded matching use hard-caps at the first apron and cannot finish above it; cap-room absorption does not. Cash and exceptions stay out. Payroll/apron values use the warehouse salary ledger as a proxy for exact Apron Team Salary; bonus, dead-money, roster-status, exception-inventory, free-agent/tender, and offseason adjustments are not computable, so apron and hard-cap conclusions are screening estimates near either apron. Legality rows expose matching_structure, matching_mechanisms, expanded_required, and a matching_note inferred as the least restrictive available simultaneous structure; they do not model actual trade-call exception elections or prior hard-cap history.
tools.schema_description: CBA trade legality check under 2023 CBA apron and salary matching rules. Payroll/apron values are a salary-ledger proxy for exact Apron Team Salary, so apron and hard-cap conclusions are screening estimates near either apron. Rows expose the inferred least-restrictive simultaneous matching structure and whether expanded matching is required.
guidelines: Use to test whether a named two-team player trade is CBA-legal under the simplified 2023 rules. Do not use for value, picks, or transactions; inputs are comma-separated player names and output is legality/matching diagnostics, not a recommended trade.

tools.name: get_trade_legality
tools.description: Trade legality verdict across 2+ teams. "legs" is a JSON array: [{"from":"BOS","to":"DEN","players":"Jayson Tatum, Sam Hauser","picks":[{"year":2028,"round":1,"protection":"top-4"},{"year":2030,"round":1,"swap":true}]}]. Optional "sign_and_trade" = {"player":"...","new_salary":15000000,"years":3} (positive salary, 3-4 season term, BYC handled; first-season full guarantee required by 2023 CBA Art. VII sec. 8(e)(1) is not validated; prior-team and preseason eligibility not modeled; years is treated as total declared seasons; non-option seasons cannot be distinguished, so option-year treatment is unsupported), "cash" = [{"from","to","amount"}] with positive integer amounts between trade parties, "tpe" = [{"team","amount","kind":"ordinary|sign_and_trade","origin_season":"YYYY-YY","origin_date":"YYYY-MM-DD","expiry_date":"YYYY-MM-DD"}]; rows are declared uses, not inventory. TPE kind is optional: ordinary accepts the standard alias, and sign_and_trade accepts sign_and_trade_generated, snt and snt_generated. Use origin_season in consecutive-year YYYY-YY form or origin_year as the season-start year; they must agree if both are present. Optional origin_date and expiry_date use YYYY-MM-DD exact dates; origin_date uses the July-June league-year calendar, must agree with origin_year/origin_season when both are supplied, and derives a one-year expiry when expiry_date is omitted. Explicit expiry_date must be after origin_date. Present keys must be non-null, and amount/origin_year must be JSON integers, so bool/float values are rejected. Amount-only legacy rows default to ordinary current-season uses and return legacy_defaults. Optional evaluation_date is YYYY-MM-DD and defaults to the league date in America/New_York. Exact expiry deadlines remain usable through their dates and expire only afterward; weekend and federal-holiday deadlines roll to the following business day. Season-only rows keep conservative legacy season bins and are explicitly approximate. At season grain, current and prior season origins are active, older entries expire, and future entries are unavailable. Each active row is a separate amount+$250k capacity bin, with the cushion reduced to $0 over the first apron. TPEs cannot combine with player salary or each other for one acquisition. Outgoing first-round picks are duplicate-checked and validated at year grain against silver_future_picks when seeded; protection/swap reconciliation and pooled/conditional picks are not modeled; same-year multiple firsts are validated only at year grain because the leg input does not identify the original team of a same-year first. Checks 2023 CBA salary matching tiers, apron aggregation bans, post-trade hard caps, typed TPE restrictions, cash bans, the frozen second-apron pick, and Stepien consecutive-first rules. REACH FOR THIS for any trade-legality ask beyond a trivial two-team player swap: sign-and-trade, multi-team, picks/Stepien, apron aggregation, TPE or cash involved. For a simple two-team salary match get_trade_check is enough. Payroll/apron values use the warehouse salary ledger as a proxy for exact Apron Team Salary; bonus, dead-money, roster-status, exception-inventory, free-agent/tender, and offseason adjustments are not computable, so apron and hard-cap conclusions are screening estimates near either apron. Legality rows expose matching_structure, matching_mechanisms, expanded_required, and a matching_note inferred as the least restrictive available simultaneous structure; they do not model actual trade-call exception elections or prior hard-cap history.
tools.schema_description: Full CBA trade legality verdict for a proposed multi-team deal: salary matching tiers, apron aggregation bans, post-trade hard caps, typed TPE use restrictions, cash bans, sign-and-trade term validation, year-grain pick ownership, and Stepien pick rules. Pick ownership limitations: protection/swap reconciliation and pooled/conditional picks are not modeled; same-year multiple firsts are validated only at year grain because the leg input does not identify the original team of a same-year first. Sign-and-trade first-season full guarantee required by 2023 CBA Art. VII sec. 8(e)(1) is not validated; prior-team/preseason eligibility is not modeled; option-year treatment is unsupported. Payroll/apron values are a salary-ledger proxy for exact Apron Team Salary, so apron and hard-cap conclusions are screening estimates near either apron. Rows expose the inferred least-restrictive simultaneous matching structure and whether expanded matching is required.

when overtime is explicitly selected (periods='ot'), or when late_clock
is given without an explicit period filter), yes, no.
periods='4th' includes overtime by default; pass include_ot=no to get
exactly the 4th quarter. Zero matches return ok True with empty
aggregates and an explanatory note, never silent zeros. Results are
time-based only, never score-aware (meta.clutch_safe=false); TS% is not
shown because the table has no free-throw attempts.
tools.schema_description: Conversational shot finder: filter warehouse shots by player, team, zone, period, makes, and late-clock window with zone and period aggregates.

tools.name: search_game_logs
tools.description:
Filter game logs by stat thresholds, opponent, time, or home/away.

player: name, nickname, or id (same resolution as every other tool).
Required unless league_wide=True or team_wide=True.
league_wide: when True, ignore player and return per-player match
counts across the whole warehouse (answers "who had the most
50-point games this season").
team_wide: when True, ignore player and return per-team match
counts across the whole warehouse (answers "which team had the
most 50-point games this season"). Each matched game counts for
the team the player was on that night (first token of MATCHUP,
e.g. "LAL vs. BOS" -> "LAL"), so a mid-season trade attributes
each game to the team at game time, not the current team.
playoffs: when True, read silver_playoff_gamelogs instead of the
regular-season table.
min_points / min_rebounds / min_assists: per-game stat floors
(e.g. min_points=40 for 40-point games). min_pra: points + rebounds
+ assists floor. max_points / max_rebounds / max_assists: per-game
stat ceilings, exclusive (max_points=20 keeps 0-19 games -
"under 20"). triple_double / double_double: keep only games
with 10+ in 3 (or 2) of PTS/REB/AST/STL/BLK. opponent: team name or
abbreviation, e.g. "Knicks" or "NYK". month: name, number, or
YYYY-MM. start_date / end_date: YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. home_away:
"home" or "away". season: 2025-26 only in the warehouse.
best_game: when True, ignore the limit and return only the single
highest-scoring game (answers "best game" / "career high" phrasing).
Returns matching games, most recent first, with the total match
count (rows beyond limit are counted, not returned). A player with
no rows in the chosen scope is an explicit ok:False error, never a
silent 0.
Warehouse only; 2025-26 only.

tools.name: get_free_agents
tools.description: Free agency and cap planning: the upcoming free agent class by team or league-wide (UFA, player/team options, two-way), estimated cap holds, and each team's projected cap room and exceptions for the next cap season. Warehouse only; refresh with seed_free_agents.py. Hold and cap figures are CBA-formula estimates, marked ESTIMATED. REACH FOR THIS for any 'who is a free agent' or 'who has cap space' ask: 'top 2027 free agents', 'which teams can offer a max slot?', 'who are the Nets' free agents?' It returns the FA list plus each team's projected room/tax/apron lines in one call - do not assemble this from get_cap_ledger, which only shows one team's current committed salary. For one team's keep-vs-renounce decision tree use get_fa_plan; for hypothetical signing amounts use get_cap_scenario.

Holds are CBA-formula estimates with per-input exactness/provenance and disclosed inference. Scenario rows expose retained/renounced unknown-hold counts, label known-dollar partial sums, and null exact projected room while unknown-amount holds remain retained. Warehouse only; refresh with seed_free_agents.py. REACH FOR THIS for any forward-looking free-agency or cap-space decision ask: 'can the Lakers keep Reaves and still sign a wing?', 'what is Boston's cap room if they renounce X?', 'walk me the Knicks' 2027 offseason.' It returns the answer-shaped scenario table directly, so do not rebuild hold/room arithmetic from get_cap_ledger or get_cap_table - those show current committed salary only and cannot answer keep-vs-renounce questions. Pair with get_free_agents for the league-wide class and get_cap_scenario for explicit hypothetical signing amounts.
tools.schema_description: Free-agent and extension planning for one team's upcoming FA class: per-FA rows (type, prior salary, estimated cap hold, extension eligibility) plus a deterministic scenario table (keep all holds / renounce all / per-player renounce or keep-only) against projected cap room and exceptions, with unknown-hold counts and partial-sum semantics disclosed.
